entries.name: Metadata
entries.text:
Artist: Nina Simone
Song: I Wish I Knew How It Would Feel to Be Free
Date: 1968
Location: The Village Gate, New York City, NY
Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SzEDYoE7YQ4

entries.name: Description
entries.text: A dark square image with Nina Simone's silhouette leaning to the left, head low, the arch of her neck centered in the frame against a deep charcoal background. In the center, a square of iridescent holographic distortion covers roughly half the image, rendering the original warm tones as shifting silver, blue, and white with subtle rainbow interference patterns.

entries.name: Details
entries.text: Recorded at The Village Gate nightclub in Greenwich Village, New York City, circa 1968. The Village Gate was a landmark jazz and folk venue that operated from 1958 to 1993 at the corner of Bleecker and Thompson Streets. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Village_Gate

entries.name: Metadata
entries.text:
Artist: Mdou Moctar
Song: Maheyega Assouf Igan
Date: 2012
Location: Tchin-Tabaraden, Niger
Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jYJGP0FBaT0

entries.name: Description
entries.text: A warm square photograph of Mdou Moctar playing an electric guitar in formal Saharan clothing, surrounded by people dancing outdoors in the dark under harsh directional lighting. The veil combine creates a soft double-exposure effect — a translucent ghost of the same scene is laid over itself, blending the warm oranges, browns, and earth tones into a diffuse dreamlike doubling across the full image. There is no distinct distortion region or noise.

entries.name: Details
entries.text: Filmed at a private wedding in Tchin-Tabaraden, Moctar's hometown in the Tahoua Region of Niger. Uploaded to YouTube on April 13, 2012. The footage was documented by Sahel Sounds and helped introduce Moctar to international audiences. http://tropicalizer.blogspot.com/2013/10/guitarist-mdou-moctar-at-wedding-in.html

entries.name: Metadata
entries.text:
Artist: Anohni
Song: If It Be Your Will
Date: January 28–30, 2005
Location: Sydney Opera House, Sydney, Australia
Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1MDlMdu2gjw

entries.name: Description
entries.text: Medium-long shot high angle of Anohni Hegarty singing on stage. Blobs and splotches of white yellow magenta lime and blue distort the entire image.

entries.name: Details
entries.text: Recorded at the Concert Hall of the Sydney Opera House as part of 'Came So Far for Beauty,' a Leonard Cohen tribute concert produced by Hal Willner for the Sydney Festival. The concert ran January 28–30, 2005. Footage was filmed for the 2005 documentary Leonard Cohen: I'm Your Man, directed by Lian Lunson. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonard_Cohen:_I%27m_Your_Man https://www.setlist.fm/setlist/various-artists/2005/concert-hall-sydney-opera-house-sydney-australia-7393d6e5.html

entries.name: Metadata
entries.text:
Artist: J Dilla
Song: F*ck the Police
Date: May 1, 2004
Location: Jazz Cafe, London, England
Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_6GX7RoSXR8

entries.name: Description
entries.text: A lofi close-up of J Dilla holding a microphone to his mouth, looking left, wearing a ballcap in a live stage setting. The midpoint combine and angled traversal have cast the entire image in a uniform cool blue-gray wash — there is no distinct distortion region, just a smooth blue-toned rendering of the original low-resolution footage.

entries.name: Details
entries.text: Performed at the Jazz Cafe in Camden, London on May 1, 2004 — one of Dilla's rare documented live appearances. The Jazz Cafe is a 440-capacity intimate venue known for jazz and hip-hop. https://www.setlist.fm/setlist/j-dilla/2004/jazz-cafe-london-england-53b573b5.html

entries.name: Metadata
entries.text:
Artist: Ted Hawkins
Song: Just One Look
Date: 1990
Location: Venice Beach Boardwalk, Los Angeles, CA
Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iy9JL_FKnW4

entries.name: Description
entries.text: A medium VHS-recorded shot of Ted Hawkins sitting on a makeshift stool on the Venice Beach boardwalk, longsleeve shirt, ballcap, acoustic guitar in hand. The cropped letters 'Ed Hawk' can be seen in tall handwriting on a open guitar case on the right side of the image on the ground. The image is sunlit high contrast with a lot of white and green. In the center is a square covering half the image with intense red, blue, yellow, and green noise.

entries.name: Details
entries.text: Recorded on the Venice Beach Boardwalk, where Hawkins was a fixture as a street performer in the late 1980s and early 1990s following his return from a period living in England. His boardwalk performances from this era were later compiled on the albums 'On the Boardwalk (The Venice Beach Tapes)' and 'Songs from Venice Beach.' https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Hawkins

entries.name: Metadata
entries.text:
Artist: R.L. Burnside
Song: Wood-Chopping Holler
Date: August 28, 1978
Location: Independence, Tate County, MS
Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2vy0dMXhlWI

entries.name: Description
entries.text: Medium shot of R.L. Burnside standing over a long log in a yard holding an axe, surrounded by grass and trees. The image is VHS-recorded with saturated greens. In the center is a square covering roughly a third of the image with red-orange distortion and teal-cyan edging, creating a heat-signature-like overlay over his figure.

entries.name: Details
entries.text: Filmed on August 28, 1978 at Burnside's farm in Independence, Tate County, Mississippi, by Alan Lomax, Worth Long, and John Bishop as part of the American Patchwork documentary project. Documented as Burnside's first film appearance. https://archive.culturalequity.org/film-and-video/american-patchwork/rl-burnsides-wood-chopping-holler-1978

entries.name: Metadata
entries.text:
Artist: The Staple Singers
Song: Sit Down Servant
Date: 1960s
Location: Unknown
Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YxgZuE14he8

entries.name: Description
entries.text: A close-up of Mavis Staples singing with her mouth open, eyes closed, hands raised open at shoulder height. The outer image is dark grayscale. The additive channel operations create a large deep indigo-blue square covering the center, with yellow-green coloration visible on her face and skin within it. The contrast between the blue field and warm yellow-green undertones gives the image an otherworldly quality.

entries.name: Details
entries.text: A television broadcast, likely from the early 1960s. The specific program has not been confirmed, but the Staple Singers were regular guests on Jubilee Showcase, a gospel music program on WLS-TV (ABC's Chicago affiliate, Channel 7) that ran from 1963 to 1984 and is the most likely context for this appearance. https://www.jubileeshowcase.com/featured_gospel_artists.html

entries.name: Metadata
entries.text:
Artist: Janie Hunter and the Moving Star Hall Singers
Song: Jonah
Date: August 1983
Location: Moving Star Hall, Johns Island, SC
Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3yG2z6GC4Ww

entries.name: Description
entries.text: A close-up of Janie Hunter and other Moving Star Hall singers, shot on VHS. The image is predominantly dark navy blue — the stacked channel operations (midpoint, xor, echo) render the scene in very low contrast, with figures barely discernible in the deep murk. The effect is subdued and somber rather than bright, giving the image an almost underwater quality.

entries.name: Details
entries.text: Filmed by Alan Lomax and crew at Moving Star Hall on Johns Island, South Carolina, in August 1983, as part of the American Patchwork documentary series. Moving Star Hall is a historic praise house central to the Gullah Geechee community. https://archive.culturalequity.org/film-and-video/american-patchwork/janie-hunter-and-moving-star-hall-singers-jonah-1983

entries.name: Metadata
entries.text:
Artist: Cameron Winter
Song: Love Takes Miles / Drinking Age
Date: January 18, 2025
Location: Sleeping Village, Chicago, IL
Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rU4BRPRlNn0

entries.name: Description
entries.text: A medium shot of Cameron Winter playing an upright piano on a spotlit stage, facing to the left and away from the audience. He is wearing a white T-shirt, there are two directional microphones hovering above the piano like antennae, facing down. The back of the heads of many audience members are at the base of the image. A centered distortion square covers two thirds of the image increasing the presence of reds on the primarily blue and white image.

entries.name: Details
entries.text: Recorded at Sleeping Village in the Avondale neighborhood of Chicago, Illinois, on January 18, 2025. https://www.setlist.fm/setlist/cameron-winter/2025/sleeping-village-chicago-il-5b5f6728.html

entries.name: Metadata
entries.text:
Artist: Sufjan Stevens
Song: Seven Swans
Date: July 16, 2016
Location: Union Park, Chicago, IL
Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nP6AIXTSqsM

entries.name: Description
entries.text: A heavily distorted image with Sufjan Stevens' face at the lower center — cap on, singing into a microphone, arms raised bearing angel wings. The spiral traversal and difference combine fracture and displace the photo into a radiating mandala-like pattern of torn fragments in blues, cyans, beiges, and oranges. A ghostlike inverted reflection of his head appears above him, and the wings create large mirrored shapes extending toward the corners.

entries.name: Details
entries.text: Performed at the Pitchfork Music Festival on July 16, 2016 (Day 2 of the three-day festival) at Union Park, Chicago. https://www.setlist.fm/setlist/sufjan-stevens/2016/union-park-chicago-il-73ff36c5.html https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork_Music_Festival_2016

entries.name: Metadata
entries.text:
Artist: Aretha Franklin
Song: Amazing Grace
Date: January 13–14, 1972
Location: New Temple Missionary Baptist Church, Los Angeles, CA
Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CBKwV6oNYvw

entries.name: Description
entries.text: A medium shot of Aretha Franklin singing into a microphone at a church podium, wearing a light-colored outfit. Behind her, robed choir members fill the frame alongside other musicians; an American flag is visible in the upper right. A large centered square covering roughly half the image is filled with intense magenta and lime green distortion, inverting and oversaturating the original warm film tones where Aretha stands. The outer edges of the image retain the natural color of the church setting.

entries.name: Details
entries.text: Recorded over two nights — January 13 and 14, 1972 — at New Temple Missionary Baptist Church in the Watts neighborhood of Los Angeles, with Reverend James Cleveland and the Southern California Community Choir. Produced by Jerry Wexler for Atlantic Records. The sessions were also filmed by Sydney Pollack; that footage was eventually released as the documentary Amazing Grace in 2018. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazing_Grace_(Aretha_Franklin_album)

entries.name: Metadata
entries.text:
Artist: Paul Robeson
Song: Ol' Man River
Date: 1949
Location: Warsaw, Poland
Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iEQEeNhtosg

entries.name: Description
entries.text: A black and white close-up of Paul Robeson's face with his mouth wide open in song, doubled horizontally across the frame. The mirror-x keymap creates a bilateral diptych — his face is reflected so two nearly identical open-mouthed singing faces appear side by side, giving the grainy television image an uncanny symmetry.

entries.name: Details
entries.text: Archival footage compiled in 'Paul Robeson: Tribute to an Artist' (1979), a documentary short directed by Saul J. Turell and narrated by Sidney Poitier. The performance clip is allegedly from Robeson's European concert tour in Warsaw, 1949. The documentary traces his evolving performances of 'Ol' Man River' — from Oscar Hammerstein's original text to Robeson's own protest rewrite. Won the Academy Award for Documentary Short Subject at the 52nd Academy Awards (1980). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Robeson:_Tribute_to_an_Artist https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0079704/ https://archive.org/details/paul-robeson-tribute-to-an-artist https://www.criterion.com/films/808-paul-robeson-tribute-to-an-artist

entries.name: Metadata
entries.text:
Artist: Pete Seeger
Song: Which Side Are You On?
Date: 1968
Location: Sweden
Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mbyaliQP-x0

entries.name: Description
entries.text: A full-image blue rendering — the echo and midpoint channel operations have cast the entire photograph in deep indigo and cobalt blue. The underlying image shows a man playing an electric guitar, body angled back with the neck raised upward, performing with audience members behind him. Faint yellow-gold details emerge through the blue suggesting stage lighting, and the guitar's frets and tuning pegs are faintly visible.

entries.name: Details
entries.text: Recorded in Sweden in 1968. Part of a documented series of approximately 14 tracks recorded on this trip, sometimes listed as 'Pete Seeger: Sweden 1968.' Whether it was a concert or a television/radio broadcast has not been confirmed; specific city and venue are unknown. https://www.last.fm/music/Pete+Seeger/Sweden+1968

entries.name: Metadata
entries.text:
Artist: Emahoy Tsege Mariam Gebru
Song: Tezeta
Date: July 12, 2008
Location: Washington DC Jewish Community Center, Washington, DC
Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SNW5T-t40sU

entries.name: Description
entries.text: A small, intimate image of an elderly woman seated at a grand piano, shown in profile facing right with her hands on the keys and sheet music on the stand. The room is very dark. Subtle patches of teal and blue-green distortion appear in the upper left of the frame, slightly shifting the ambient cool darkness of the room. The effect is restrained, preserving much of the original image's quiet atmosphere.

entries.name: Details
entries.text: Benefit concert on July 12, 2008 at the Washington DC Jewish Community Center (DCJCC). Proceeds supported the Emahoy Tsege Mariam Music (ETM) Foundation. Widely described as her first public performance in 35 years. http://www.tadias.com/07/08/2008/historic-concert-by-ethiopian-nun-pianist-composer-in-dc/

entries.name: Metadata
entries.text:
Artist: Jason Molina
Song: Hold On Magnolia
Date: December 3, 2006
Location: Acme Comics & Records, Columbia, SC
Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YQtjwVTJUgw

entries.name: Description
entries.text: A medium shot of Jason Molina seated at a microphone, head bowed downward, in a record store — shelves of records and posters visible in the background. A large orange-red rectangle covers the central two-thirds of the image in warm distortion. Within the rectangle, two small isolated bright blocks appear — one pale blue and one yellow — like corrupted color artifacts against the orange wash. The outer edges retain the natural warm brown tones of the shop.

entries.name: Details
entries.text: Soundboard recording (Track 6 of 17) taped by '2000 Flushes' at Acme Comics & Records in Columbia, South Carolina, on December 3, 2006, during Molina's fall 2006 American solo tour. https://jasonmolina.com/tour-archive/2006 https://content.jasonmolina.org/post/22261565741/live-from-south-carolina-jason-molina

entries.name: Metadata
entries.text:
Artist: Burning Spear
Song: Jah No Dead
Date: 1978
Location: Jamaica
Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sGQlDLBRKAU

entries.name: Description
entries.text: A dim, low-contrast performance photograph showing several figures in a dark indoor setting. A centered deep violet-purple square covers the middle third of the image, rendering the figures within it as blue-purple shapes with faint lime-yellow highlights. To the left, a figure in light blue clothing is visible outside the distortion. The surrounding image is dark and muted with warm reddish ambient light.

entries.name: Details
entries.text: A scene from Rockers (1978), directed by Ted Bafaloukos and shot entirely on location in Jamaica. The 'Jah No Dead' sequence was filmed at the ruins of a colonial-era jailhouse near the sea. The song was composed specifically for the film. Leroy 'Horsemouth' Wallace plays the lead character. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockers_(1978_film)
